title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on the Work of Selection and Appointment of Judges of Intellectual Property Courts (Trial)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Judges of Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation)

Fa [2014] No. 267

To the Higher People's Courts of Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangdong Province:

The Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Judges of Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation) are hereby issued for your diligent implementation.

October 28, 2014

Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Judges of Intellectual Property Courts (For Trial Implementation)

Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the PRC, the Judges Law of the PRC, the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Establishment of Intellectual Property Courts in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, and the Framework Opinion of the Central Committee on Several Issues Concerning the Pilot Reform of the Judicial System, and in light of the actual work of intellectual property adjudication, these Guiding Opinions on the Selection and Appointment of Judges of Intellectual Property Courts are formulated as follows:

1. The selection and appointment of judges of intellectual property courts shall adhere to the principles of Party management of cadres, open selection, and emphasis on actual performance, and shall highlight the professional characteristics of intellectual property adjudication.

2. The judges of intellectual property courts shall be selected and appointed openly in accordance with the provisions of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the PRC and the Judges Law of the PRC. Among them, the selection and appointment of presidents, vice presidents, and division chiefs shall be organized in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations on the Selection and Appointment of Party and Government Leading Cadres.

3. The judges of intellectual property courts shall be selected and appointed from among outstanding adjudicators engaged in intellectual property and related adjudication work, and may also be selected and appointed from among professionals engaged in intellectual property legal practice, legal research, and legal education who possess equivalent qualifications and conditions.

4. Adjudicators serving as judges of intellectual property courts shall meet the qualification requirements prescribed by the Judges Law of the PRC and also satisfy the following conditions:

(1) Hold the qualification of Grade 4 Senior Judge;

(2) Have more than 6 years of relevant adjudication work experience;

(3) Hold a bachelor's degree or above in law from an ordinary institution of higher education;

(4) Have strong ability to preside over court hearings and draft adjudicative documents.

5. For other legal professionals serving as judges of intellectual property courts, the qualifications and conditions may be set by each locality by reference to these Opinions.

6. The Judge Selection Committee shall review the professional competence of judge candidates and propose candidates in a differential manner based on the review results.

7. The investigation work on candidates for the positions of president, vice president, division chief, and judge of intellectual property courts shall be jointly undertaken by the organizational and personnel departments and the disciplinary inspection and supervision departments.

8. After the candidate for president of an intellectual property court is determined, the chairperson of the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the city where the court is located shall submit the nomination to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level for appointment.

After the candidates for other adjudicative positions are determined, the president of the intellectual property court shall submit the nominations to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level for appointment.

9. The selection and appointment of judges of intellectual property courts shall be conducted under the leadership of the Higher People's Court of the locality, and major issues shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court, the local Party committee, and the political and legal affairs committee.
